Hi Alex — thanks for the inventory. Quick read-through looks good; a few missing pieces that we’ll need before we schedule a day-zero smoke run: 

Action items / preflight checklist (please flag anything you can’t provide right away):
1) Network diagram (layer 2/3) with CIDR ranges and transit/peering approach (VPC peering vs TGW).
2) Bastion/jump host access plan and preferred auth method (SSO/SSH keys).
3) KMS key ARN(s) and whether rotation is managed by MediNova.
4) Service account model: list of service accounts and scopes for Redwood to call (if any).
5) Egress allowlist: app-level outbound destinations (Dest IPs/FQDNs) and ports.
6) Expected traffic profile (RPS, typical sequence length, peak window).

From Redwood side, Karthik will own the network/security acceptance and will share our minimal firewall port matrix + sampling of required IAM bindings. Kimberly will coordinate the onboarding timeline and contract MOPs.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the network diagram and confirm KMS ARNs by EOD Friday (6/20).
- We send an intake packet (template) with exact firewall/egress rules and a list of required ports.
- Schedule a 60-min technical walkthrough next week with your infra and security teams.

Forwarding the attached inventory to Karthik and Kimberly for the technical checklist.

Best,

Thanks for the inventory, Alex — pasted below is a compact technical acceptance checklist we’ll use to validate the environment. Naomi, feel free to add schedule notes.

Redwood minimal tech acceptance checklist (high level):
- Network & routing:
  • CIDR ranges for all subnets and the desired peering topology (VPC peering vs TGW).
  • NAT/eip plan for egress (if any) and whether egress traffic must come from static IPs.
  • MTU and any enforced VLAN tagging across the private link.
- Firewall / ports (sample):
  • Outbound: 443 to *.redwood.ai (TLS), 5228/5229 to internal telemetry endpoints (when enabled).
  • Inbound to enclave: minimal — Redwood initiates outbound connections; if you require inbound callbacks, list exact ports.
- Identity & secrets:
  • KMS ARN(s) and whether key policy allows Redwood principal (if not, we require envelope encryption instructions).
  • Service account JSON / IAM role names for cross-account access (if AWS).
- Bastion and access model:
  • Preferred session manager (SSM) vs SSH jump host with MFA.
  • Jump host IP allowlist and rotation cadence.
- Telemetry & logging:
  • Splunk HTTP ingest endpoint or S3 path; retention and retention policy.
  • Audit log export window for at least 90 days for initial acceptance.
- Smoke/runbook requirements:
  • A host (or /24) available for smoke traffic generation and one ops engineer during the run.

Please attach the network diagram and confirm whether the KMS key is customer-owned with Redwood read-only permissions or fully managed by MediNova. If you need our acceptance matrix as a spreadsheet, say the word and I’ll attach it.
